title: The footprint of climate oscillations in global inland waters: analysis code and derived data
description:
Reproducible analysis quantifying how the leading modes of interannual climate variability (ENSO, IOD and NAO) explain year-to-year temperature variability in global rivers and lakes (surface and bottom), on a common 0.5° grid, 1950–2021.

The oscillation footprint F is the fraction of detrended interannual water-temperature variance jointly explained by the three modes (adjusted R² of a multiple regression on the season-specific, standardised indices); grid cells where F is field-significant (Benjamini–Hochberg FDR < 0.05) are termed teleconnected. Two-block variation partitioning separates a direct/memory pathway from a locally-mediated one. This deposit contains the R analysis code, derived GeoTIFF/JSON products, figures and self-contained interactive tools (including a live walkthrough of the F computation).

See the repository README and input/DATA_SOURCES.md for full provenance and reproduction instructions.
